# Native decoder notices

This offline bundle accompanies Sharp 0.35.5 and `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64` 1.3.4. Original notice, copyright, authorship and license bytes are stored once under their SHA-256 names. `manifest.json` maps every original path to those unchanged bytes, source URL, archive checksum or pinned upstream Git association. The production image retains this directory alongside the installed packages' original notices.

There are 28 versioned native components and 29 rows in the upstream native notice mapping: libnsgif is vendored within libvips 8.18.7 and its original COPYING is explicitly associated. The 357 registry crates conservatively cover the exact librsvg 2.63.2 Cargo.lock, including development and other-platform dependencies. In total, 803 original references map to 343 unique texts (1,656,228 bytes). This is broader than the installed Linux binary dependency set and is not an exact production SBOM or legal completeness attestation.

Some published crates have no standalone LICENSE. Their original Cargo declarations and notice-bearing source/README bytes are retained with corresponding full license texts and upstream version/commit associations; the manifest records where association uses a workspace tag rather than a published archive's VCS identity. No copyright attribution is invented. FreeType's FTL and GPLv2 texts and full GNU GPLv3/LGPLv3, MIT, Apache-2.0 and MPL-2.0 bodies are included.

Normal tests and production rehearsal use `deploy/development/manual-native-notices.mjs` entirely offline to verify all byte hashes, file sets, counts, associations and substantive full-license sections. Updating the decoder requires reviewing its installed `versions.json`, upstream `sharp-libvips` build tag, source archives/checksums and package notices, then replacing the bundle and its pinned assertions together. Provenance URLs are rebuild references, never runtime fetches. The official upstream build scripts and release sources recorded in the manifest provide source/build references; this bundle is not a claim of a bit-reproducible native rebuild. Applications needing a different native build can use Sharp's documented custom libvips installation/build path at https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com/install/.
